tagline: Turn a policy requirement into a scan-ready .audit file.
lore: Draco, the Athenian lawgiver who set down the first written code — here he turns a policy requirement into a written, enforceable Tenable .audit check.
problem: Every organization has requirements no stock benchmark covers — a registry value, a config line, a service that must never run. Writing them as Nessus .audit checks means learning a strict grammar by trial and error, and one quoting mistake stops the file from loading.
does: Draco writes custom Tenable .audit files two ways: describe the check in plain English and an AI model drafts Nessus checks, or build each check field by field from a platform catalog. Every file is previewed live, syntax-validated and mapped to frameworks before you download it — and you can seed a whole CIS benchmark and adjust it in one prompt.

glance.caption: Draco's builder: a check described in plain English, the drafted <custom_item>, its framework references, and the live .audit preview with validation.

capabilities: "password minimum length must be 14 on Windows servers" becomes drafted checks you can edit; with no AI model configured it says so and the builder still works.

Windows config (registry, password, lockout and audit policy, user rights, services, REG_CHECK, WMI, PowerShell), Windows file content, and Unix / Linux / macOS (file, content, command, RPM, process, service).
start from the built-in control index for CIS Docker, Ubuntu Linux or RHEL and tighten sections in one prompt — "create a CIS Docker benchmark and tighten 5.x".
the .audit grammar is checked so the file loads into a compliance scan.
NIST, PCI, HIPAA, CIS and ISO references suggested for each check.
upload an existing .audit; each <custom_item> is kept verbatim and becomes editable.
how: Draco writes nothing to Tenable or navi — the .audit file is built and downloaded in your browser. The benchmark library holds control numbers, short titles and framework mappings, not CIS text; verify numbering against the official benchmark before an assessment.
who: Compliance engineers and auditors who need custom checks, and platform owners turning internal standards into something a scan can test.
better: Upload Draco's file to a Tenable compliance scan; once results sync into navi.db, Minos judges them across the estate and Tiresias explains them asset by asset.
cta: Tell Draco the rule — he writes the law your scanner can enforce.
